title: Entropy-based ingest batcher and correlation repair for structured logs
creator: Asha Banerjee
description:
Problem: We see intermittent bursts of structured log loss and unlinked traces during tenant rebalancing and transient network partitions. Root cause analysis from recent incidents shows: occasional missing correlation fields from older SDKs, out-of-order delivery across Kafka partitions, and high-cardinality fields causing routing hotspots. Existing ingest path assumes a stable corr_id and strict schema; when either is absent the log is dropped or indexed with garbage, making latency/error dashboards and trace joins unreliable.

Goal: Implement an ingest-side 'entropy batcher' that groups and orders events adaptively using probabilistic bucketing and a downstream 'correlation repairer' that reconstructs or synthesizes provenance for logs missing corr_id/trace pointers while preserving auditability and minimizing false joins.
proposal:
1) Add a lightweight batching layer in the ingest proxy (Vector sidecar component) that assigns logs to 'entropy buckets' computed from a tenant-scoped hash of stable fields (tenant_id + service + minute-bucket). The batcher will maintain per-bucket ordering windows and emit monotonic sequence tokens to downstream Kafka topics.

2) Implement a correlation-repair microservice in the ingestion cluster that:
  - ingests ordered batches from the specialized Kafka topic,
  - attempts deterministic reconstruction of corr_id using traceable fingerprints (span hashes, request path, consistent user identifiers),
  - when deterministic repair is impossible, issues a synthetic corr_id with provenance metadata (repair_reason, reconstruction_score) and marks records as 'repaired' for downstream consumers.

3) Schema fallback: the repairer will also try adaptive schema mapping for legacy agents by applying a prioritized set of field-mappers and a lightweight inference pass before re-indexing to Loki/ELK.

4) Backpressure and circuit: batcher will expose a per-tenant circuit-breaker to spill to cold-storage when repair queue latency exceeds SLOs, preventing cascade failures in indexers.
design_notes:
- Entropy bucketing minimizes cross-partition reordering while keeping batch sizes small; chosen hash: murmur3(tenant|service|floor(ts/60)).
- Sequence token format: v1:{bucket}:{seq_no}:{emitter_epoch} (string) to avoid binary metadata in Kafka keys.
- Reconstruction heuristics: prefer deterministic (span-hash + client-ip + request-id) -> if score >= 0.85 accept; else produce synthetic id and attach repair_score.
- Audit trail: every repaired record includes repair.producer (service name), repair.reason, repair.score, and original_raw_id (if present). These fields are stored in Loki as labels and in ELK as top-level fields for easier filtering.
- Privacy: synthetic corr_ids are UUIDv4 prefixed with tenant salt and a one-way HMAC to avoid exposing internal identifiers. Key management uses existing KMS integration from Private deployments.
- Telemetry: new metrics exported to Prometheus: "ingest.batcher.emit_latency_ms", "ingest.repair.success_rate", "ingest.repair.false_positive_estimate", and histograms for reconstruction score distribution.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype batcher as a Vector transform in staging (2 sprints).
Phase 2: Correlation-repair microservice + schema fallback library with unit tests (3 sprints).
Phase 3: Integrate Kafka topic routing and update consumers (indexers) to respect sequence tokens (1 sprint).
Phase 4: Canary rollout to 10% tenants with live dashboards and auto-rollback policy (1 sprint).
Phase 5: Full rollout with operator runbook and backfill tools (1 sprint).
tasks: ENG: add Vector transform (entropy-batcher) and feature flag integration (repo: infra/observability).
ENG: implement repairer service with REST + consumer group (repo: services/log-repair).
ENG: add sequence-token parser to indexers and update Loki label enrichment (repo: indexers/loki-writer).
QA: fuzz test reconstruction heuristics with synthetic missing-corr workloads.
SRE: create Grafana dashboard panels and Prometheus alert rules for repairer SLOs.
SEC: confirm KMS HMAC usage and validate PII handling for synthetic ids.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for batcher hashing and sequence token generation.
- Integration tests across Vector -> Kafka -> repairer -> Loki/ELK in a dedicated pipeline.
- Fuzz corpus derived from historical 30-day sample (anonymized) to estimate false-positive repair rate; target <0.5%.
- Load test at 3x expected peak ingestion to validate queue sizing and backpressure behavior.
- Chaos test: simulate partition reassignment and node restart to verify monotonic sequence tokens prevent item loss or duplication.
rollout_plan: 1) Enable feature flag in staging for internal tenant. 2) Canary to 5% production tenants (low QPS) for 72h with automatic rollback on repair.false_positive_estimate > 0.8% or repairer.queue_latency_p99 > 2s. 3) Gradually increase to 30% then 100% following health checks. 4) Run nightly backfill to repair historical logs for tenants opting in. 5) Post-rollout audit and retention of repair metadata for 90 days.
monitoring:
- Grafana dashboard: repairer success rate, reconstruction score histogram, batcher emit latency, per-tenant backpressure state.
- Alerts: P0 if repairer error-rate > 5% sustained for 5m, P1 if queue latency p99 > 2s.
- Logs: repairer emits structured 'repair.event' records with original_labels and repair.* primitives.
- SLOs: target end-to-end (ingest->index) median added latency < 40ms for unrepaired, < 120ms for repaired; p99 < 1s for unrepaired, < 3s for repaired.
acceptance_criteria:
- Prototype batcher reduces cross-partition reordering by >= 70% on sample trace.
- Repairer deterministic success >= 85% and overall false-positive rate < 0.5% on fuzz corpus.
- No increase in dropped logs during canary; indexer error-rate unchanged.
- Prometheus metrics instrumented and Grafana dashboards present.
- Runbook and rollback tested and documented.
- Security signoff for synthetic ID generation and storage of repair metadata.
open_blockers: Confirm Kafka retention strategy for the new sequence-topic with data privacy team (PR open: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/412).
Finalize KMS HMAC policy — awaiting security review (ticket SEC-221).
Need small-capacity dedicated queue for repairer in staging (SRE approval).
